text:
Trent Frederic had a telling week. Oilers Nation wrote on Nov. 4 about "Frederic stepping up for teammates," and four days later The Hockey Writers' weekly preview led with him being scratched. That's the bind for a physical bottom-six forward who isn't scoring: the hits (35 in 15 games) only buy so much ice time.

One goal is his total, and he's gone 10 straight games without a point. Some of that is finishing. His 1.74 individual expected goals (the quality of his own chances) say he's about a goal light, and he's shooting 6.7%, below the 9 to 14% range we'd expect from him. The five-on-five picture is the bigger concern: Edmonton gets 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly eight points worse than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had a hopeful note from last season: he gets shots off passes across the slot or from behind the net (1.6 per 60), the kind that go in far more often. But his first full Oilers season brought 4 goals and 3 assists in 74 games, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level. Those slot passes need to start turning into goals.
headline: Trent Frederic's scoring has gone quiet
